name: Iris
grown_as: The bearded iris of cottage gardens. ⚠️ CHECK: William's library has two irises: 'Grandma's', 0.6 to 1 m tall in the Upper Orchard, which fits a bearded iris and is drawn here; and Iris reticulata 'Pauline', a dwarf iris 10 to 20 cm from a true bulb, violet-purple with a white mark on the falls, with narrow four-sided leaves, flowering in February. They look very different. The colour of 'Grandma's' is not known: drawn as the classic old purple bearded iris.
habit: Clumps of stiff, flat fans of sword-shaped leaves 30 to 60 cm high, from thick rhizomes lying on the soil surface, with branched flower stems 60 to 100 cm tall above.

leaf.arrangement: In flat fans: each leaf folded lengthways and sitting astride the next (equitant), all in one plane
leaf.outline: 30 to 45 cm long by 2.5 to 4 cm wide, the sides straight and parallel, curving to the tip
leaf.base: Overlapping in the fan, often tinged purple
leaf.veins: Many fine parallel veins, no strong midrib
leaf.surface: Smooth, stiff, with a grey waxy bloom

flower.form: Three falls hanging down, three standards upright, a fuzzy beard on each fall
flower.petals: Six tepals. Three outer 'falls', broad, hanging down and outwards. Three inner 'standards', upright and arching in over the centre. Three petal-like style arms arch over the base of each fall.
flower.colour: Violet-purple (variety): falls deeper red-purple, standards lighter violet
flower.centre: A beard of fuzzy hairs, yellow or white tipped yellow, down the middle of the upper part of each fall; veining at the base of the falls
flower.behind: A green and papery spathe at the base of each flower
flower.carried: Two to five flowers on a branched stem above the leaves, upright

fruit: Rarely set in gardens. When it is: a large three-sided green capsule 5 to 7 cm, splitting into three to show brown seeds.
seedling: Not drawn: grown by dividing rhizomes.
winter: Short fans of leaves, the outer ones brown and dead, on rhizomes showing at the soil surface.

leaf: a flat sword-shaped leaf with straight parallel sides
grey-green, fine parallel veins, no strong midrib
bloom: three broad falls hanging down and three standards upright
a fuzzy yellow beard on each fall
petal-like style arms arching over the falls
bulb: a rhizome, not a bulb: a thick knobbly brown stem lying flat on the soil, half above it
ringed with old leaf scars, roots underneath
a fan of leaves at its growing end
shoots: flat fans of grey-green sword leaves from the rhizome
leaves folded and sitting astride each other in one flat plane
flower: branched stems taller than the leaves with several bearded flowers
seedhead: a large three-sided pod on the stem
dormant: short fans of leaves, outer ones brown

look_alikes: Yellow iris has no beard, small standards and green leaves with a raised midrib. Siberian iris has no beard and narrow grassy leaves. Iris reticulata is tiny, from a bulb, with four-sided leaves. Fans of leaves look like gladiolus or crocosmia, whose leaves are ribbed or pleated.
